I farm only 4.1 mu, so I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation that I already know and can manage well. Since some people in my household work off-farm, I will choose a simple and reliable way to farm, not something that needs too much extra labor. I have well irrigation, so I will use water at the key stages instead of depending only on rainfall. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put on enough nitrogen for steady tillering and grain filling, and add phosphorus and some potassium because the land is used continuously and I do not want the soil to weaken. I will till with rotary tillage because it is practical on my small area and fits how I manage residue and sowing. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want strong yield from my limited land. I will give maize more nitrogen than wheat, keep phosphorus and potassium at moderate levels, and irrigate at the important stages if rain is not enough. I will not spray too many times, only enough to control the usual weeds, insects, and diseases, because I want to control cost and labor while protecting yield.
